headline: A Home Rule Petition letting the city use its own money to repair unaccepted roads was approved.
summary: The petition covers unaccepted ways that the public uses, not private ways. Residents on a street would need to want the work and petition the city to move it along. Building permit fee changes, a permitting software contract, and four solar net metering agreements were also approved.
decisions: Approved reappointing Dominique Pierre-Louis as constable, 8 yes.
Approved a vehicle-for-hire license for Monumental Black Car Services, 8 yes.
Approved a vehicle-for-hire license for Bhamra Corporation, 8 yes.
Approved $43,858.47 for Springbrook utility billing and tax collection maintenance, 8 yes.
Approved a three-year online permitting software contract with Vertosoft, $311,148.96 in year one, 7 yes and 1 no.
Approved a net metering credit sales agreement with Logging Swamp Solar LLC, 7 yes and 1 no.
Approved a net metering credit sales agreement with Clems Way Solar LLC, 7 yes and 1 no.
Approved a net metering credit sales agreement with NW Plymouth Street Solar LLC, 7 yes and 1 no.
Approved a second net metering credit sales agreement with Logging Swamp Solar LLC, 7 yes and 1 no.
Approved accepting a $36,000 recycling dividends grant, 8 yes.
Approved transferring $33,000 from the Edwin J. Castle Fund for awards, 7 yes and 1 abstention.
Approved a Home Rule Petition on maintenance of unaccepted ways, 8 yes.
Approved accepting a $10,998.16 FY 2027 Student Awareness Fire Education grant, 8 yes.
Approved accepting a $4,200 FY 2027 Senior SAFE grant, 8 yes.
Approved transferring $15,411.92 from the Edwin J. Castle Fund for awards, 8 yes.
Approved an ordinance updating building permit fees, 7 yes and 1 abstention.
discussion: Unaccepted ways petition: Members said many homeowners did not know their street was unaccepted when they bought, and that the petition would let the city use its own CIP money to fix roads instead of filling potholes.

Net metering solar agreements: The developer's presentation estimated year-one savings of about $276,000, at no cost to the city, against about 13 million kilowatt hours of use. Members asked what happens if the solar farms produce less, and were told the city would pay only for what is produced.

Permitting software contract: Members said some residents find the current site hard to use, and asked whether other options cost less. The mayor said the city has found OpenGov meets its needs for now, and may look at other options later.

GIC health coverage move: The mayor said 788 active employees and 785 retirees enrolled, with a January start date. The mayor's report said the change would save tens of millions of dollars over the long run.

Searles Estate insurance: Members asked why HUB International charges of $107,063.92 and $100,998.64 did not appear in FY 2027. The CAFO said the estate is essentially self-insured for now, and a planned insurance bid would seek coverage at a lower price than for other city buildings.
